summary.one_liner: A Claude Code/Codex/Cursor skill that writes, fixes, and validates OpenTelemetry Collector configs, encoding common Collector pitfalls as a checklist.
summary.what_it_does: It is a single SKILL.md agent skill (plus reference docs, examples, and a validation script) that guides an AI agent in producing OpenTelemetry Collector YAML. It turns plain-English requirements into a commented config, or diagnoses a pasted broken config with a what's-wrong, why, and fix breakdown. The skill checks for specific failure modes such as processor ordering (memory_limiter before batch), core vs contrib component availability, pull vs push metric exporters, removed or deprecated exporters, and receivers defined but never wired into a pipeline. The references/components.md file catalogs receivers, processors, exporters, and connectors with their gotchas, and references/advanced.md covers OTTL, spanmetrics, tail_sampling, and exporter reliability. The README says the agent finishes by running otelcol validate, and scripts/validate.sh wraps that command, auto-detecting contrib and falling back to Docker. Example configs include a broken-to-fixed pair and an advanced spanmetrics config.
use_cases: write an OpenTelemetry Collector config from a plain-English description
diagnose why no telemetry reaches a backend
fix a broken otelcol YAML config
validate a Collector config before deploying
choose between prometheus and prometheusremotewrite exporters
check processor ordering in a Collector pipeline
notable: Encodes concrete Collector footguns (processor order, contrib-only components, pull vs push exporters) as an agent checklist
Validation loop: the agent runs otelcol validate before declaring a config done
Includes a broken-to-fixed example config pair walking through five bugs
Vendor-neutral scope covering OTLP, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, and Mimir export
Works with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor via a plain SKILL.md file
caveats: Focused only on Collector config; does not cover instrumentation SDKs or dashboards
Some configs require the contrib image, so the core build will not run them
The README says a capable model already knows much of this; the value is consistency and the validation loop
